description: Prediction — distance to a win, and the hands a partial tray can still become.

entries.title: An empty tray predicts nothing
entries.cite: The panel has nothing to work from; saying anything would be inventing a plan.

entries.title: Four tiles is too few to name a plan
entries.cite: SPARSE_BELOW — under five tiles a hand is compatible with almost every shape in the game.

entries.title: Five tiles is enough to start naming hands
entries.cite: SPARSE_BELOW is five: at five tiles the shapes have begun to separate.

entries.title: A finished hand has nothing left to predict
entries.cite: Prediction is about what is missing. Nothing is.

entries.title: An empty tray on a Hong Kong table behaves the same
entries.cite: Variant-independent: the state machine is about how much is keyed.

entries.title: Three tiles short of a Full Flush, and it says which three
entries.cite: TT — the archived Tabletopia Singapore ruleset §Full Flush (清一色): 'four points'. RULING R3 prices the flush; R4a is what stops Pure Green stacking on top of it.

entries.title: Two dragon pungs and a dragon pair are three tiles from Three Great Scholars
entries.cite: TT — the archived Tabletopia Singapore ruleset §Three Great Scholars (大三元): 'this criterion is often awarded the limit'. RULING R8b — a limit award prices the whole hand.
entries.note: The third dragon completes 大三元 and the odd chow finishes the hand.

entries.title: A hand of terminals and honours is offered Thirteen Wonders
entries.cite: TT — the archived Tabletopia Singapore ruleset §Thirteen Wonders (十三幺): awarded the limit. RULING R12 is about how it is PAID, not what it scores.

entries.title: A claimed meld leaves three sets to find, not four
entries.cite: The concealed target is 14 minus the tiles already on the table.

entries.title: An exposed kong makes the concealed hand one tile longer
entries.cite: RULING R14 and src/engine/core/hand.ts — a winning hand is 14 tiles plus one for every kong, because a kong is four tiles doing the work of three.
entries.note: Eleven concealed tiles plus a four-tile kong is fifteen on the table, which is fourteen plus one for the kong.

entries.title: Never asks for a fifth copy of a tile
entries.cite: Four of each tile exist. A suggestion that needs a fifth is not a suggestion.

entries.title: Never asks for a tile the melds have used up
entries.cite: Three copies of 9m are on the table; only one can ever come back.

entries.title: A sequence hand is only worth its four tai on the right wait
entries.cite: TT — the archived Tabletopia Singapore ruleset §Sequence Hand (平胡): 'four points'. RULING R5 — the wait must be two-sided or wider on a discard, and an all-chow hand that forfeits it scores nothing at all.
entries.note: This is the entry that would have caught the winning-tile defect: the plain sequence hand pays 4 on some finishes and is not a legal win on others, so the panel must quote a range, not a number.

entries.title: Nine Gates is offered to a one-suit hand that has the shape for it
entries.cite: TT — the archived Tabletopia Singapore ruleset §Nine Gates (九蓮寶燈): awarded the limit.

entries.title: One tile from 坎坎糊, and it says which
entries.cite: RULING-LOG-HK.md HK9/HK21 — 坎坎糊 8, and HK21: every set a pung or kong with none of them claimed. HK8a 門前清 1, 無花 1.
entries.note: Concealed all the way through, so HK21 makes it 坎坎糊 rather than 對對糊. The entry pins the distance and the tile; the fan is pinned by the certification invariant against every way it can finish.

entries.title: A one-suit Hong Kong hand is offered 清一色
entries.cite: RULING-LOG-HK.md HK8a — 清一色 7, 平糊 1, 無花 1 — and HK12, 門前清 1, which Hong Kong scores on a discard.
entries.note: 7 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 10, which is also the default cap. The point of the entry is that the panel quotes the whole hand, not just the flush.

entries.title: Hong Kong is never offered an animal tile
entries.cite: RULING-LOG-HK.md HK1 — 144 tiles, and the animals are Singapore's.

entries.title: A hand that cannot reach three faan is not offered as a plan
entries.cite: RULING-LOG-HK.md HK2 三番起糊 — a hand below the minimum is not a legal win, so it is not a suggestion.

entries.title: Hong Kong offers 十三么 from a spread of terminals and honours
entries.cite: RULING-LOG-HK.md HK8b 十三么 例牌.

entries.title: The cap a table plays changes what a plan is worth
entries.cite: RULING-LOG-HK.md HK3 — the cap is a setting; a 例牌 shows 13 at a 13-faan cap and 10 at the default.

entries.title: The same hand at the default cap is worth ten
entries.cite: RULING-LOG-HK.md HK3 — ten faan is the Hong Kong Mahjong Association's cap and the default.

entries.title: A Hong Kong hand with a claimed meld still counts to fourteen
entries.cite: RULING-LOG-HK.md HK1.

entries.title: Flowers in the tray do not change what the tiles can become
entries.cite: RULING-LOG-HK.md HK8a — the flower lines score, but they are not part of the tile hand.

entries.title: A Singapore hand of the same tiles predicts differently
entries.cite: The two variants score the same tiles differently, so they plan differently. TT — the archived Tabletopia Singapore ruleset §Full Flush 4 tai vs RULING-LOG-HK.md HK8a 清一色 7.

entries.title: A hand one tile from home says one tile
entries.cite: The distance is the number of tiles still to acquire, nothing more.

entries.title: A hand needing a discard says what to drop
entries.cite: A plan that keeps every tile is rare; the panel has to name the odd one out.
entries.note: Three loose tiles in three different suits cannot all become a set and an eye in two draws, so every plan has to drop something.

entries.title: A hand with three melds down is predicted, not written off
entries.cite: A three-meld hand needs five concealed tiles. Comparing the concealed count against a fixed threshold meant it could never be predicted at all, however close to home it was.
entries.note: Four keyed tiles, and the hand is one tile from Three Great Scholars.

entries.title: A dragon already claimed still counts towards the dragon hands
entries.cite: TT — the archived Tabletopia Singapore ruleset §Three Great Scholars (大三元). A pung on the table is IN the hand; asking for three more copies of it deleted the archetype for exactly the players who were halfway there.

includes.needed: F F F P P P

entries.note: Five keyed tiles, a dragon already on the table, and the two remaining dragons are the whole distance. Before the fix this archetype forced three MORE copies of the melded 中 into the concealed hand, found only one left in the game, and returned nothing — so every dragon and wind hand vanished for exactly the players holding one.

entries.title: Hong Kong's ordinary concealed hand is offered, because 自摸 is counted
entries.cite: RULING-LOG-HK.md HK8a — 平糊 1, 自摸 1, 門前清 1, 無花 1 — and HK2, three faan to win. Scored only as a discard the hand reaches 3 and the panel could not offer it; on a self-draw it is 4.
entries.note: The most ordinary tray in the game. Before the fix the panel offered it four limit hands eight to eleven tiles away and not this.

entries.title: Singapore's Hidden Treasure needs a self-draw, so it is quoted as one
entries.cite: TT — the archived Tabletopia Singapore ruleset §Hidden Treasure (四暗刻): all triplets, concealed, self-drawn — awarded the limit.
entries.note: Priced as a discard win the same tiles are worth 2. The panel now says both: the floor it pays however it lands, and the limit it reaches if drawn.

entries.title: A Hong Kong hand that the flowers already won says so
entries.cite: RULING-LOG-HK.md HK8b — 「集齊七隻花牌可即時食糊」. The deal ends the moment the seventh flower is drawn.
entries.note: Telling this player they are nine tiles from winning would be nonsense: they have won.

entries.title: Fourteen tiles that are not a hand are not called finished
entries.cite: The state was a size test. A tray of fourteen unrelated tiles is the likeliest mistake at a table, and it was being told to go and score.

entries.title: A wind pung is offered, because it is the cheapest fan there is
entries.cite: RULING-LOG-HK.md HK8a — 門風 1, 圈風 1, and 「門風及圈風重疊時計兩番」 when they are the same wind. It is the standard way a Hong Kong hand clears three faan.
entries.note: East seat in the East round, so the pair of East is worth two faan once it is a pung.

entries.title: A fourth copy is a kong waiting to be declared, not a tile to throw
entries.cite: Candidate.discard is documented as tiles the hand has no room for. A fourth copy sitting on a triplet is not that.

entries.title: The sparse hints only promise fan for honours that pay
entries.cite: RULING-LOG-HK.md HK8a — a dragon triplet scores, and so does the seat or round wind. A triplet of any other wind is worth nothing in either variant, and the hint says "real fan".
entries.note: One of these four honours pays: the 中. West and North are neither the seat nor the round wind here.

entries.title: The same tiles are a limit hand drawn and two tai claimed, and the panel says both
entries.cite: TT §Hidden Treasure (四暗刻): all triplets, concealed, SELF-DRAWN — awarded the limit. TT §Triplets Hand (碰碰胡): two points. RULING R8b.
entries.note: The floor is what it pays if somebody throws the last tile; the ceiling is what it pays if it is drawn. Quoting either one alone would be a false statement, which is why the panel quotes the range and names the condition.
